messages:
alex: Heads up — after the 17:02 canary deploy charts (sparklines) are stuttering on high-card pages. CPU spikes in the renderer, main thread ok but worker threads climb memory then crash. :eyes:

maria: seeing same on EU canary, +1. timeline shows long parse/compile for vendor~web...chunk (1.2MB gz) right after route change.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-21T17:02 UTC started by @maria. https://deploys.internal/redwood/console/canary/527

jay: got heap profile — worker heap grows ~80MB -> 200MB over ~30s on open heatmap page. suspect the new telemetry serializer (batching) changed to inline SourceMap parsing in the worker.

alex: here's quick repro: open /dash?panel=heatmap then click "stream" mode. run DevTools -> Profiles -> Record Allocation. Also see console warning: "Prefer streaming parser; fallback to parseAll()"

maria: config diff from canary: telemetry.sampling for "widget-exec" changed from 0.02 -> 0.5 and prefetch.batchSize 4 -> 8. cc @jay

jay: that explains it — sampling spike will massively increase payload + stringify cost. Also prefetch batch bump means more simultaneous worker jobs. We also shipped new vendor lib 'fast-json-parse' inlined.

sam: can we flip telemetry sampling back to 0.02 for canary? Or gate it behind feature flag? We need to know perf impact vs value.

deploy-bot: Patch 527.2 created to revert telemetry sampling. rollouts: canary -> 10% -> 50%

priya: here's a tiny patch you can apply locally to test: 
```js
// disable heavy telemetry in dev
window.__REDWOOD_FEAT__.telemetryWidgetExecSampling = 0.02;
```

alex: tried the revert on a canary node, memory stops climbing and sparklines smooth out. Confirmed.

jay: long term: we should avoid stringify-heavy work in ui-worker. Move to a streaming encoder in main thread or use smaller proto format. Also add a soft cap on prefetch concurrency per widget.

maria: proposed quick mitigation: revert sampling + revert prefetch.batchSize to 4 + hotfix to lazy-import fast-json-parse behind a dynamic import.

sam: agree. Can someone open a small RFC outlining changes to routing/quota interaction with telemetry? This feels like an architecture smell where observability config can blow up client cost.

alex: opening RFC in a sec. For now I'll approve the patch rollback. :shipit: 

priya: thumbs up from me. Also adding an observability test that asserts no worker heap growth > 60MB for 30s on critical pages.

jay: created issue #C-4212 to track long-term work (streaming encoder, proto, prefetch backpressure). https://issues.redwood/C-4212

maria: patch deployed to canary revert; monitoring: cpu and worker heap trending back to normal. closing.
